title: Play and amusement
hookLine: this life is play, amusement, adornment, boasting, and rivalry in wealth (57:20)

lines: THE RIGHT OUTFIT. THE NEW CAR.
cards: A toddler with a plastic bucket on the beach. A teenager scrolling at midnight. A thirty-year-old choosing the right outfit for a wedding.
A forty-year-old mentioning, casually, the new car. A seventy-year-old counting grandchildren and property. Five people wanting five different things.
Surah Al-Hadid, verse twenty, lines up five words in a row, and some commentators have read them as exactly that: one life, from the beach to the end.

teach.b: Pickthall: "Know that the life of the world is only play, and idle talk, and pageantry, and boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children".
In Arabic, the five are la'ib, play; lahw, amusement or diversion; zina, adornment; tafakhur, boasting to one another; and takathur, piling up more wealth and children than the next person.
Some commentators noticed the order follows the stages of a life: the child plays, the youth is diverted, the young adult adorns, the grown person boasts, the old person counts what they've gathered.
Then a picture: rain brings up plants that delight the farmer. Then they dry, turn yellow, and become straw.
Green, yellow, straw: the life of the world in one season.
And in the next verse, a turn: race one another toward forgiveness from your Lord, and a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth. Is the verse against fun? The hadith collections suggest not.
Bukhari records that the Prophet ﷺ let 'A'isha watch a group of Abyssinians performing with spears in the mosque on a feast day, standing so she could see over his shoulder until she'd had enough.
The verse isn't banning the beach bucket. It's naming what play is: lovely, and passing, like grass after rain. Its warning is against mistaking it for the whole of life.

how: Muslim preachers often recite 57:20 in reminders about the passing nature of worldly life, while the hadith tradition also preserves room for play, sport and celebration, especially on the two Eids.

games.q: it's a feast day, and a group of Abyssinians are performing with spears in the mosque. 'A'isha wants to watch. what does the Prophet do?
o: stands so she can watch over his shoulder.
games.why: he let her watch, standing so she could see, until she'd had enough. the verse names play as passing, not forbidden.

practice: Think of what most often fills your spare minutes, a game, a feed, a show, a habit of checking, and without judging it, picture setting it down for an hour.
Then picture what might fill that hour instead: a walk, a person, a page, a prayer if you pray.

wordCard.voice: Lahw: amusement, diversion, one of the five words Surah Al-Hadid uses for the passing life of the world. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: play and amusement, the first two of the five words of 57:20.
